messages:
alex_w: Thinking out loud — what if instead of a single linear percent ramp for model swaps we used a small lattice of parallel cohorts with staggered holdpoints?

mira: Can you sketch what the lattice looks like? is this different from cohort waves + canary steps?

sam_g: quick note: we need to keep it simple for Console UX. customers rarely want >3 knobs.

alex_w: Agreed re UX. Proposal: base lanes = [baseline, safety, experimental]. Each lane has its own percent curve but traffic assigned via a lattice mapping that ensures safety lane always has rollback rights and quota headroom.

mira: Example config? even pseudo-YAML helps.

alex_w: Paste draft config: 
```yaml
rollout: 
  id: model-v2-lattice-2026-03
  lanes:
    baseline:
      target: 70
      schedule: [0, 10, 30, 50, 70]
      holdpoints: [0, 600, 1800, 3600, 7200]
    safety:
      target: 20
      schedule: [0, 5, 10, 15, 20]
      holdpoints: [0, 300, 900, 1800, 3600]
    experimental:
      target: 10
      schedule: [0, 1, 2, 5, 10]
      holdpoints: [0, 120, 600, 1200, 2400]
  lattice_mapping: 
    - cohort: region-a
      lanes: [baseline, safety]
    - cohort: region-b
      lanes: [baseline, experimental]
  guards:
    error_rate_threshold: 0.02
    p95_latency_ms: 800
    quota_buffer: 0.15
```

katie_p: Nice. The lattice mapping is interesting — ensures we don’t put experimental into every cohort at once. Two quick asks: 1) how do we compute "quota_buffer"? 2) how do rollbacks propagate across lanes?

ryan_ops: For rollback propagation, we should have an explicit policy: fence(experimental)->pause(safety)->fallback(baseline). In practise that means experimental failures trigger safety holdpoint and console shows a single-click rollback that drains experimental then reduces safety if needed.

sam_g: UI thing: console should present the lanes as toggles with a compact sparkline for each lane (errors / cost / qps) and a single master percent slider that maps to lattice mapping under the hood.

alex_w: quota_buffer = fraction of reserved capacity per lane to avoid soft OOM when cohort spikes. default 0.15 but computed from historical peak QPS * 1.2 factor.

mira: telemetry hooks we need: per-lane traces, per-cohort error counters, and a cross-lane reconciliation metric (named lattice_fanout_ratio). Also surface an aggregate early-warning alert if lattice_fanout_ratio deviates > 35% from training baseline.

deploy-bot: deploy queued: rollout/model-v2-lattice-2026-03 -> scheduled at 2026-03-21T09:00Z :rocket:

katie_p: One more: safety lane should be first-class in API. Expose a param lane_priority so SDKs can request cost vs safety tradeoffs (e.g. lane_priority=safety for critical customers).

ryan_ops: Ops note: make sure autoscaling policy is lane-aware. if safety hits quota_buffer, autoscaler should prioritize safety nodes within the cohort.

alex_w: Cool. Next steps: I'll update the RFC with the lattice YAML and add an example console mock. Who wants to review?

mira: I'll take the API section. sam_g can you review the UX copy?

sam_g: Yup.

katie_p: I'll validate alert thresholds with SRE numbers.

alex_w: Thanks all. Marking action items in the RFC. :thumbsup:
